query: The Faculty Basket {Up the hollow middle of the Lecture Tower runs a wicker basket on a rope, for faculty knees. A sign says FACULTY ONLY. It's two hundred and twelve steps to the top.|The basket is waiting at the bottom again. Someone has added "AND THEIR LUGGAGE" to the sign.|The basket. You know its creak, its sway, and the exact landing where it likes to stop.} {Professor Thorne's satchel is riding up in it, alone.|It still smells faintly of Professor Vey's perfume.|{season == "summer": The stairwell is an oven by the fifth landing.|A draught howls up the stairwell like a chimney.}} Ride it up, quietly {You ride up beside the satchel, which seems to disapprove, and step off at the top fresh as morning.|You glide past six landings and step out at the top as if you'd walked. Your knees send their thanks.|The basket stops where it likes to stop; you know the trick of the rope now, and arrive at the top unwinded and unseen.} {The satchel's owner is waiting at the top. Thorne looks at you, then at the sign. "Hm." You walk back down, then up.|The basket stops between floors. Professor Vey leans over the rail above. "Faculty," she says, "are generally taller." It's ten minutes before anyone winds you down.|It sticks at its favourite landing, and a whole lecture hall files past, one by one, to look at you.} Climb all two hundred steps {You arrive at the top red-faced and righteous, legs like wet bread.|You count the steps aloud. Somewhere beside you the basket creaks past, empty, smug.|You take the steps two at a time now, and only stop to breathe at the landing where the basket stops.}
